done_when: Every reported surface has a source-clean candidate, exact blocker, or accepted public readback.
The Fusha fixtures fail if a finite verb hides prefix, root, form, person, number, or object suffix.
The Fusha fixtures fail if a preposition, function particle, host, or attached pronoun is hidden inside a stem segment.
The Fusha fixtures fail if a common particle such as هَلْ, مَا, وَمَا, or إِنَّكُم remains draft-only while solved peers exist.
The Qamus executor treats same-surface rich peers as transclusion candidates, not optional hints.
A page cannot be called visually complete while Plan 17 false-closure findings or Fusha flywheel rows remain unaccounted.
five_whys: Visible public qwords were counted as handled while they remained draft-only, flat, or undersegmented.
Packet/accounting outputs were not enough; every visible cited-card qword needs public DOM readback.
The audit did not make same-surface rich peers, known finite-verb morphology, and attached suffix/pronoun morphology mandatory enough.
Transclusion evidence was advisory instead of a repair-or-exception gate.
Reusable sarf/nahw lessons needed exact fixtures, procedures, validator queues, drills, and installed-skill reminders.
